hypotheses.rationale: Histone machinery disorders frequently overlap in intellectual disability and facial dysmorphism. Distinguishing KDM6B disorder from Kabuki syndrome (KDM6A/KMT2D) relies on whether classic Kabuki hallmarks like lateral palpebral eversion and fetal pads are strictly absent or occasionally present due to shared chromatin-modifier pathways.

evidence.text: Histone-related disorder reviews describe classic Kabuki syndrome features including persistent fetal fingertip pads and lower eyelid eversion alongside KDM6B-associated neurodevelopmental conditions, highlighting the differential overlap among histone methylation disorders.

hypotheses.text: Distal skeletal anomalies in KDM6B-related disorder are confined to non-specific mild findings (such as fifth-finger clinodactyly or brachydactyly) and completely lack fifth digit distal phalanx or nail hypoplasia/aplasia (HP:0001792), providing 100% specificity against Coffin-Siris syndrome.
hypotheses.rationale: OMIM designates the KDM6B phenotype as 'neurodevelopmental disorder with coarse facies and mild distal skeletal abnormalities'. Delineating whether 'mild distal skeletal abnormalities' ever includes fifth digit hypoplasia is critical for clinical differentiation from SWI/SNF-complex chromatinopathies such as Coffin-Siris syndrome.

evidence.text: OMIM classifies heterozygous variants in KDM6B as producing neurodevelopmental disorder with coarse facies and mild distal skeletal abnormalities, rather than the severe distal digit/nail aplasia typical of Coffin-Siris syndrome.

hypotheses.text: The occurrence of palpebral fissure elongation in KDM6B patients is accompanied by neutral or upslanted fissures without lateral eversion, making the specific configuration of the palpebral fissure a decisive discriminator between KDM6B and KDM6A/Kabuki syndrome.
hypotheses.rationale: Elongated palpebral fissures are reported across histone methylation disorders, but lateral ectropion/eversion of the outer lower eyelid is believed to be restricted to Kabuki syndrome. Verifying that KDM6B patients do not show eversion despite elongated palpebral fissures provides a granular physical exam discriminator.

evidence.text: Discussions of histone methylation syndromes note elongated palpebral fissures alongside eversion of the lateral third of the lower eyelid in the spectrum of epigenetic disorders, though KDM6B-specific phenotypic delineation requires isolating whether eversion specifically occurs.
